questions.question: Who has the power to grant pardons?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President **__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Article 72 **of the Constitution **empowers the President to reduce the punishment **of a person or to **grant pardon.**
 
• The President may grant pardon i.e. suspension of sentence, sentence adjournment, relief, and pardon.
 
• **The Governor **of the state has also been granted the **"power of pardon" by Article 161 **of the Constitution.
 
• **The governor does not have the right to pardon the death penalty.**
 
• The Governor can reduce the death penalty by suspending the death penalty and change the nature of the punishment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Under Article 72 of the constitution of India President has the power to Pardon, Commute, Remit, Respite and Reprieve the sentence. 

 
• Pardon - President can pardon the sentence of any convicted person and bring him to the position where all his deeds of crime will not carry any punishment. 
 
• Commute - President can reward lesser punishment to the person in place of rigorous punishment.
 
• Remit - by remitting the power President lessen the term of imprisonment. 
 
• Respite - In this, the President considers some cases and decrease the punishment of the offender. 
 
• Reprieve - In case of a death sentence, the President can hold the punishment.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles mentions that the state shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 14**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 14** of the Constitution of **India states that the state shall not deny any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.**
 
• **Article 14 is divided into two parts: **
 
• **Equality before the law**
 
 
• This part states that everyone should be treated equally in the eyes of the law.
 
 
 
• **Equal protection of the laws**
 
 
• This part states that the same law will be applied to all people equally across society.
 
 
 
• The** phrase "equality before law" originated in England,** while "**equal protection of law" comes from the American Constitution.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Article 12:-

 
 
• The word 'State' is defined under Article 12 of the Indian Constitution, which includes the Government and Parliament of India, the Government and Legislature of each of the States, and all local or other authorities within the territory of India or under the control of the Government of India.
 
• The scope of the word 'State' has been expanded by the judiciary to include private bodies or individuals performing public functions, which has led to the application of Fundamental Rights against them as well. 
 
 
 
• Article 15:-
 
 
• It prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
 
 
• Article 13:-
 
 
• It declares that any law that violates the Fundamental Rights shall be void.

questions.question: Who among the following social reformers of British India was known as Lokhitwadi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Gopal Hari Deshmukh.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Gopal Hari Deshmukh (1823-1892) was a social reformer and rationalist from Maharashtra.
 
• He held the post of a judge under the British raj but wrote for a weekly Prabhakar under the pen name of Lokahitawadi on social reform issues.
 
• He wrote 'Shatpatre' in the Prabhakar newspaper. In 'Shatapatre' he wrote about Political, Religious, Social, Cultural topics.
 
• He was against Child Marriage, the Dowry system, Polygamy.
 
• He also criticized the Caste System in society.
 
• He was a supporter of Girls Education.
 
• He advocated a reorganization of Indian society on rational principles and modern, humanistic, secular values.
 
• He attacked Hindu orthodoxy and supported social and religious equality.
 
• **After bearing public criticism he served lame, blind and leprosy persons. **
 
• He wrote against the evils of the caste system. He said, “If religion does not sanction social reform, then change religion”.
 
• He started a weekly, "Hitechhu", and also played a leading role in founding the periodicals, Gyan Prakash, Indu Prakash, and Lokahitawadi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jyotiba Phule****​**

 
 
• Jyotirao Phule was a social reformer, activist, and writer who lived in the 19th century in Maharashtra, India.
 
• He founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873 with the aim of uplifting the lower castes and women through education and social reforms.
 
• The Satyashodhak Samaj was a movement that challenged the caste system and advocated for social equality and justice.
 
• Jyotirao Phule was also a strong advocate of women's education and established the first school for girls in Pune in 1848.
 
 
 
• **Veeresalingam Pantu**lu ​
 
 
• Veeresalingam Pantulu (16 April 1848 – 27 May 1919) was a famous social reformer and writer of the modern period of Telugu literature.
 
• He was known by the title 'Gadya Tikkana' and was often considered 'Raja Ram Mohan Roy' of Andhra.
 
• Born in a Brahmin family, Veeresalingam Pantalu was a staunch opponent of the caste system and started the anti-caste movement.
 
• He established widow ashrams and formed an association for Widow Remarriage in Madras Presidency.
 
• To encourage women's education, he established schools for girls in 1874 at Dowlaiswaram near Rajahmundry.
 
• Veeresalingam Pantulu earned a reputation as the first novelist, the first playwright, and the originator of modern journalism.

questions.question: How many fundamental duties were enumerated in the 42nd Amendment of the Constitution?

__
 
• 10 Fundamental duties added in** Part IV(A) **of the Indian constitution by **42ⁿd Amendment Act, 1976**.
 
• Added three words to the Preamble by same Amendment, **"Socialist, Secular, and Integrity".**
 
• Fundamental duties are listed in **Article 51A **of the Constitution of India.
 
• **11th** Fundamental Duty is added by **86th Amendment Act of 2002.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **42ⁿd Amendment** increased duration of Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies from **5 to 6 years**(Later removed by 44th Amendment Act.) 
 
• Gave the Central Government more control over the **appointment of State Governors.**
 
• **Introduced** provisions for establishing **Administrative Tribunals( Article 323A and 323B)** to handle dispute related to services.
 
• It is also known as** "Mini Constitution"**
 
• Added a provision that any law passed by the Parliament related to amendment** cannot be questionable **in any court **[ Article368(4) ]**.
 
• **Introduced Part XIV** A to the Constitution, which deals with Tribunals of** Administrative disputes and Service related disputes**.
 
• **Limited Right to Property under Article 19(1)(f) **and removed it as fundamental right, **later fully removed by 44th Amendment Act**.
 
• **Indira Gandhi was the Prime Minister** of India during 42ⁿd Amendment Act.

questions.question: Which natural form of vitamin B helps to prevent some of the major birth defects of the baby's brain (anencephaly) and spina bifida?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Folate**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Folate** (vitamin B9) **is the natural form of vitamin B that can help prevent birth defects **like anencephaly and spina bifida: 
 
• **Folic acid can reduce the risk **of neural tube defects (NTDs), which include anencephaly and spina bifida, by more than 70%.
 
• NTDs occur when the spinal cord doesn't close properly. 
 
• The **CDC recommends that all women of reproductive age take 400 micrograms (mcg) of folic acid daily before and during early pregnancy. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anencephaly **is a** serious birth defect where parts of the baby's brain and skull don't form properly, **and babies born with it cannot survive.

 
 
• The upper part of the neural tube does not close fully during early embryonic development.
 
• Adequate intake of folic acid before and during early pregnancy can reduce the risk.
 
 
 
• Spina bifida is another serious birth defect where the baby's spine doesn't develop correctly, which can lead to severe physical disabilities.
 
 
• It can range from mild (occulta, often asymptomatic) to severe forms (myelomeningocele, involving nerve damage and disabilities such as paralysis or bladder/bowel dysfunction).

questions.question: Vacuoles in plant cells can occupy up to what percentage of the cell's volume?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 90**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Vacuoles are organelles of **plant, fungal, and algal cells**.
 
• They are part of the internal membrane system and are separated from the rest of the cytoplasm by a membrane called the** tonoplast.**
 
• Vacuoles play crucial roles in cell expansion, serve as storage compartments for nutrients, and function as lytic organelles that contain digestive enzymes.
 
• Compounds contained within vacuoles also protect cells against environmental damage and deter attack by herbivores.
 
• Vacuoles are filled with a watery fluid called **cell sap** **(made up of water, salts, and sugar).**
 
• I**n some plant cells, a vacuole may occupy as much as 90 per cent of a cell's total volume.**
 
• When a vacuole takes up this much space in a cell, it presses the cytoplasm (jelly-like fluid in a cell) against the cell wall, which eventually remains stretched out under this force.
 
• As long as the vacuole remains full, the plant maintains its turgor pressure (like the air pressing against the inside wall of a balloon).
 
• When the vacuole loses this fluid and decreases the pressure, it collapses temporarily and the plant wilts.
 
• Maintaining this cellular pressure is the prime responsibility of the vacuole in a mature plant.
 
• When pressure is maintained, the entire plant is able to keep its crisp shape. When it does not, the whole plant wilts. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Cell: 

 
 
• The cell is the fundamental unit of life. All the life activities are carried out by cells.
 
• The organisms are classified based on the number of cells present in them.
 
• Unicellular organisms are single-celled, while multicellular organisms have a large number of cells. 
 
• Differences between the plant cell and animal:
 
 
• ​The cell wall is present in Plant cells while it is absent in an animal cells. A cell wall gives mechanical support to a plant cell. 
 
• Plants have both a cell wall that is made up of cellulose and a cell membrane (plasma membrane). The cell wall is, a rigid membrane matrix found on the surface of all plant cells whose primary role is to protect the cell and its content. 
 
• Plant cells have a large central vacuole that can occupy up to 90% of the cell’s volume. Animal cells may have many small vacuoles, a lot smaller than the plant cell.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed in the Directive Principles of State Policy?

options.text: Promote the welfare of the people

__
 
• The** Directive Principles of State Policy, listed in Part IV** of the Indian Constitution, do not explicitly mention "rights for transgenders in certain cases."
 
• However, **it includes provisions like promoting the welfare of the people,** ensuring equal pay for equal work, and advocating for a uniform civil code.
 
• The** rights of transgender individuals have been addressed more through judicial rulings and legislative measures rather than as a specific directive principle.**

• Articles 36-51 of Part-IV of the Indian Constitution deals with Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP). 
 
• They are borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland. 
 
• DPSPs are non-justiciable i.e non-enforceable in the court of law.
 
• They act as directives to the government to create any law.
 
• There are mainly three categories of these principles – Socialist Directives, Gandhian Directives, and Liberal Intellectual Directives.

• It indicates whether the country has a surplus or a deficit in trade.
 
 
• When exports exceed imports, there is a trade surplus and when imports exceed exports there is a trade deficit.
 
 
 
 
 
• Components of BoP:
 
• For preparing BoP accounts, economic transactions between a country and the rest of the world are grouped under - Current account, Capital account, and Errors and Omissions. It also shows changes in Foreign Exchange Reserves.

• Capital Account: It confers capital expenditure and income for a country.

__
 
• According to the **Constitution of India**, the **Chief Justice of India** (CJI) is required to seek the prior permission of the **President of India** before appointing **Adhoc Judges** in the Supreme Court of India.
 
• An Ad hoc judge is a Supreme Court judge appointed by a procedure for a specific project or case for a specific period of time.
 
• **When a quorum of permanent judges is required to continue or hold a Supreme Court session, Article 127 of the Indian Constitution proposes that the Chief Justice of India can appoint a High Court judge as an ad hoc Supreme Court judge for a specified time.**
 
• **The Supreme Court Chief Justice can only do so after consulting with the Chief Justice of the High Court in question and receiving the President's prior consent.**
 
• The judge chosen for this position must be eligible to sit on the Indian Supreme Court.
 
• Above all other obligations, it is the judge so designated's responsibility to attend Supreme Court sessions.
 
• **In doing so, the Ad hoc judge in India has all of the power, authority, benefits, and obligations of a Supreme Court judge.**

• **Ad hoc Judges' Role:**

 
 
• Cases that are more than five years old are usually assigned to ad hoc judges. Regardless, it would not be inappropriate for the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court to exercise his discretion in hearing such cases.
 
• It is not necessary to form a divisional bench of Ad hoc Judges and Sitting Judges in cases to be heard before the Division Bench. At the moment, the Division Bench may only be made up of ad hoc judges because these are old cases that need to be heard.
 
 
 
• 
 Because an ad hoc judge's role is to carry out the functions of a Supreme Court Justice, it would be inappropriate for an ad hoc judge to perform any other permitted work.
